moduleTitle: Automating Mobile Apps on TMA — Part 2: Testing Native, Hybrid & Web Apps
learningObjectives: Implement advanced techniques to create and execute test scripts on native, hybrid, and web applications within Tricentis Tosca Mobile.
Build a complete TestCase against a native app, from Open Mobile App through verification.
Build a TestCase against a hybrid app that steers both native chrome and embedded webview controls in one flow.
Build a TestCase against a mobile web app running in the device's own browser.
Recognise which parts of the workflow change between the three app types, and which stay identical.

elements.term: What stays the same across all three
elements.description: Native, hybrid and mobile web tests share Tosca’s Module/TestStepValue and supported ActionMode concepts. Opening differs: native/hybrid apps use Open Mobile App after any required capability setup; websites use OpenUrl. Buffer stores data; Verify performs assertions.

Native controls use exposed platform properties. Hybrid flows combine native and web content with the appropriate context. Mobile web scanning/execution defaults to Mobile Web Engine 3.0, with version-specific legacy alternatives; it is not one identical engine path for every app type.

bulletPoints: Share modeling concepts while configuring opening, engine and context for each application type.

elements.title: End-to-end native flow
items: Configure required capabilities, then Open Mobile App with the installed-app identifiers or target-compatible installation build.
Steer each screen's scanned controls in sequence — taps, text entry via Send Text Input To Focused Control, list scrolling via Swipe On Screen where no scrollable control was captured directly.
Insert Verify TestSteps at meaningful checkpoints (a confirmation screen appearing, a field showing an expected value) rather than only at the very end.
End the current Appium session when finished and check any provider-specific reservation cleanup separately.

elements.text: Treat this sequence as independent local authoring guidance. Reliability depends on the application, identifiers, synchronization and assertions rather than an assumed reliability ranking between application types.

bulletPoints: Use meaningful assertions at checkpoints to narrow the failing operation; this does not guarantee a single root cause.

elements.term: Context switches belong in the TestCase, not just the scan
elements.description: Use Get Appium Context and Set Appium Context when the execution flow needs native/web context changes. Confirm the actual current and target contexts rather than assuming each scanned control automatically switches execution context.

elements.text: A context mismatch can prevent correct steering. Inspect the active context and errors before diagnosing the failure; neither a captured context nor an explicit switch guarantees every control operation succeeds.

Synchronize against observable readiness such as an enabled target before interacting with newly loaded content. WaitOn can wait for a property condition; a one-time Verify or buffering operation alone is not a substitute for waiting.

bulletPoints: Confirm and change contexts where the flow requires it.
Wait for a meaningful readiness condition before interacting.

elements.term: DOM steering through the Mobile Engine
elements.description: Use OpenUrl and the relevant Browser TCP for a mobile website. Tosca 2026.1 defaults mobile web scanning/execution to Mobile Web Engine 3.0; native and embedded web content have their respective engine/context behavior.

elements.title: Things that differ from a desktop XBrowser TestCase
items: Viewport and layout reflect the real device's mobile browser, not a resized desktop window — elements that reflow at mobile width need controls captured at that width, not assumed identical to desktop.
Touch-based interaction patterns (tap, swipe) apply, rather than mouse-hover-dependent behaviour a desktop site might rely on.
Browser chrome (address bar behaviour, mobile-specific prompts) is part of what's on screen and occasionally part of what needs steering.

bulletPoints: Use the documented mobile-web opening and engine path.
Validate responsive layout and interactions on the actual chosen target.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming a hybrid TestCase inherits the right context automatically
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Steering a webview-captured control right after a native-context TestStep without an explicit context switch in between.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Confirm the current Appium context and switch to the required target context when the flow needs it. Inspect errors instead of assuming captured controls automatically select the correct context.

examPitfalls.title: Steering into a webview before it's finished loading
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A hybrid TestCase intermittently fails on the first control inside freshly-navigated webview content, while later controls in the same webview work fine.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use an appropriate readiness wait such as WaitOn for the required property before interaction; a single Verify is an assertion rather than a universal wait.

examPitfalls.title: Treating mobile web like a resized desktop XBrowser TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming controls and layout captured on a desktop-width scan will match what the Mobile Scan captures at real mobile viewport width.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Scan and steer mobile web at the device's actual viewport — reflowed layouts at mobile width can present different, or differently-positioned, controls than a desktop capture would.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which three general authoring principles apply across native, hybrid and mobile web tests? (three correct answers)

options.text: Configure the appropriate opening and connection workflow for the target
TestStepValue/ActionMode mechanics for steering a Module
The need for explicit native/webview context switches
Use supported Verify assertions to check outcomes

practiceQuiz.hint: One of the four options is specific to only one of the three app types.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Each target needs suitable opening/connection setup, Module steering and assertions. Opening steps and engine paths differ; hybrid context changes are not a universal requirement. Buffering alone does not assert an outcome.

optionExplanations.A: Each target needs appropriate opening/connection setup; the exact steps differ.
optionExplanations.B: The common Tosca model uses TestStepValues and supported ActionModes.
optionExplanations.C: Native/web context switching is relevant to mixed-context flows, not all tests.
optionExplanations.D: Verify assertions check outcomes; Buffer alone stores values.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Logs show a hybrid webview target is not yet enabled when the first interaction executes. Which issue should the team address?

options.text: The control was scanned in the wrong app entirely.
Synchronize with the target’s readiness before interaction.
TMA does not support hybrid apps.

practiceQuiz.hint: The logs establish a readiness condition, not merely an unexplained intermittent failure.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The observed readiness issue calls for a suitable property wait before interaction. It does not prove all hybrid failures are timing defects or that webviews always load more slowly than native screens.

optionExplanations.A: The logs establish readiness, not scanning a different application.
optionExplanations.B: A readiness wait addresses the observed enabled-state issue.
optionExplanations.D: Storage is not the readiness cause established by these logs.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why should mobile web controls be captured at the device's actual mobile viewport, rather than reused from a desktop XBrowser scan?

options.text: XBrowser scans cannot capture web controls at all.
Layout reflows at mobile width can present different or differently-positioned controls than a desktop capture.
Native and mobile web always use identical opening Modules and engine paths
Desktop scans are always faster to execute.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about responsive layout behaviour, not engine architecture.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Responsive layouts can differ in controls and positions. Validate the mobile target; native app opening and mobile website opening/engine paths are not identical.

optionExplanations.B: Responsive layouts can change available controls and positions.
optionExplanations.C: Opening and engine paths differ by application type.
optionExplanations.D: Universal desktop speed is not established or relevant.

quickRecap.value: Common Module/ActionMode concepts; application opening and engine paths differ.
Inspect actual native identifiers and validate synchronization and assertions.
Confirm active/target contexts and wait for observable content readiness.
Use OpenUrl, the platform Browser TCP and the documented mobile-web engine.
